statements.status_notes: Apache Tomcat RCE via Default Servlet partial PUT — file fragments uploaded to predictable temp paths trigger deserialization of assembled content. Also enables reading security-sensitive files.
statements.impact_statement: Remote code execution and information disclosure via Tomcat Default Servlet partial PUT support. Requires an HTTP PUT request to a running Tomcat servlet container with partial PUT enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts the Tomcat HTTP server, never deploys any servlet, and never opens any network port. The Default Servlet, partial PUT handling, and file session persistence code paths are never activated.

statements.status_notes: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. Incorrect error handling for some invalid HTTP priority headers resulted in incomplete clean-up of the failed request which created a memory leak. A large number of such requests could trigger an OutOfMemoryException resulting in a denial of service. This issue affects Apache Tomcat from 9.0.76 through 9.0.102, from 10.1.10 through 10.1.39, from 11.0.0-M2 through 11.0.5, and 8.5.90 through 8.5.100. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.0.104, 10.1.40 or 11.0.6 which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Memory leak on invalid HTTP priority headers, fixed in Tomcat 11.0.6, 10.1.40 and 9.0.104. The upstream fix changes only Tomcat's HTTP/2 implementation (org.apache.coyote.http2), so the leak is reachable only over HTTP/2. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or newer, which include the fix. Spring Boot enables HTTP/2 only when server.http2.enabled is set; the application sets no server properties, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer, so its connector speaks HTTP/1.1 only.

statements.status_notes: Improper Neutralization of Escape, Meta, or Control Sequences vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. For a subset of unlikely rewrite rule configurations, it was possible for a specially crafted request to bypass some rewrite rules. If those rewrite rules effectively enforced security constraints, those constraints could be bypassed. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.5, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.39, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.102.
statements.impact_statement: A crafted request can bypass some rewrite rules of Tomcat's RewriteValve; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.6, 10.1.40 and 9.0.104. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs a RewriteValve with rewrite rules. Spring Boot exposes no property that enables the RewriteValve; it must be added in code through a web server factory customizer together with a rewrite configuration. The application sets no server properties, packages no rewrite.config, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer.

statements.status_notes: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's CGI servlet allows security constraint bypass of security constraints that apply to the pathInfo component of a URI mapped to the CGI servlet. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.6, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.40, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.104.
statements.impact_statement: Case-sensitivity handling in Tomcat's CGI servlet allows a bypass of security constraints on the pathInfo of a URI mapped to that servlet; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.7, 10.1.41 and 9.0.105. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs the CGI servlet to be registered and mapped. Embedded Tomcat under Spring Boot does not load Tomcat's default web.xml and never registers the CGI servlet; the application registers only Spring's DispatcherServlet and none of its classes references CGIServlet or the Tomcat API.

Denial of service via excessive memory consumption in Tomcat multipart upload processing. Requires sending a crafted multipart/form-data HTTP POST to a running Tomcat instance. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never accepts HTTP requests. The multipart parsing code path is completely inactive.

Denial of service via HTTP/2 stream reset memory leak in Tomcat. Requires an HTTP/2 connection to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and accepts no inbound network connections.

statements.status_notes: Untrusted Search Path vulnerability in Apache Tomcat installer for Windows. During installation, the Tomcat installer for Windows used icacls.exe without specifying a full path. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.7, from 10.1.0 through 10.1.41, from 9.0.23 through 9.0.105.
statements.impact_statement: The Tomcat installer for Windows ran icacls.exe without a full path during installation; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.8, 10.1.42 and 9.0.106. The flaw is in the Windows installer executable distributed with the full Tomcat server download, not in the tomcat-embed-core library. No Liquibase Secure artifact ships or runs the Tomcat Windows installer. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the 5.x license-tracking application (10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer from 5.0.3), as a library inside that application's jar; it contains no installer code.

statements.status_notes: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. When using PreResources or PostResources mounted other than at the root of the web application, it was possible to access those resources via an unexpected path. That path was likely not to be protected by the same security constraints as the expected path, allowing those security constraints to be bypassed. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.7, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.41, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.105.
statements.impact_statement: Resources mounted as PreResources or PostResources other than at the web application root could be reached through an unexpected path that bypasses security constraints; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.8, 10.1.42 and 9.0.106. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs PreResources or PostResources mounted at a non-root path. Spring Boot exposes no property for this; it requires code that customizes the Tomcat context's WebResourceRoot. Spring Boot's own Tomcat setup adds only resource-jar sets mounted at the web application root, and only for jars that contain META-INF/resources, which none of the application's libraries do. None of the application's classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer, and the application bundles no Spring Security and defines no security constraints.

Denial of service via integer overflow in Tomcat multipart upload file size limit validation. Requires sending a crafted multipart HTTP upload to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never processes inbound HTTP requests or multipart uploads.

Denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption in Tomcat HTTP/2 stream management. Requires an HTTP/2 client connecting to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and never binds a network port.

statements.status_notes: Session Fixation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat via rewrite valve. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.7, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.41, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.105.
statements.impact_statement: Session fixation through Tomcat's RewriteValve; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.8, 10.1.42 and 9.0.106. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs a RewriteValve. Spring Boot exposes no property that enables it; it must be added in code through a web server factory customizer. None of the application's classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer. The application is a stateless REST service and creates no HTTP sessions.

Path traversal and potential RCE via regression in Tomcat Rewrite Valve URL normalization. Requires an HTTP request to a running Tomcat server with the Rewrite Valve configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never configures the Rewrite Valve, and never accepts HTTP requests.

statements.status_notes: Improper Neutralization of Escape, Meta, or Control Sequences vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. Tomcat did not escape ANSI escape sequences in log messages. If Tomcat was running in a console on a Windows operating system, and the console supported ANSI escape sequences, it was possible for an attacker to use a specially crafted URL to inject ANSI escape sequences to manipulate the console and the clipboard and attempt to trick an administrator into running an attacker controlled command. While no attack vector was found, it may have been possible to mount this attack on other operating systems. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.10, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.44, from 9.0.40 through 9.0.108.
statements.impact_statement: Tomcat's log formatters did not escape ANSI escape sequences, so a crafted URL that Tomcat logs could manipulate a console that renders them; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.11, 10.1.45 and 9.0.109 by adding escaping to the JULI formatters (OneLineFormatter, JdkLoggerFormatter). The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it, and its start.bat supports running it in a Windows console. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The unescaped formatters are never used by the application: Spring Boot's Logback logging system removes the java.util.logging root handlers and installs SLF4JBridgeHandler, so every Tomcat log record is written by Logback, not by a Tomcat formatter. The application packages no logging.properties and none of its classes or libraries other than tomcat-embed-core itself references the JULI formatters.

statements.status_notes: If an error occurs while Apache Tomcat processes a multipart upload, the temporary copies of the uploaded parts are left on disk for the garbage collector to delete instead of being removed immediately, so repeated failing uploads can fill the temporary directory faster than GC clears it; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.12, 10.1.47 and 9.0.110. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz); it runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. None of the application's endpoints accepts multipart data, but that does not protect it: the application leaves Spring Boot's multipart support at its defaults (enabled, eager parsing, file-size threshold 0 bytes), so Spring's DispatcherServlet, mapped at "/", parses the body of any multipart request to any path before it looks up a handler, and Tomcat writes every part to its temporary directory. The application listens on port 8080 on all interfaces by default and has no authentication. This was established by reviewing the application's configuration and the bundled Spring Boot 3.4.2, Spring Framework 6.2.2 and Tomcat 10.1.34 code; it was not reproduced against a running instance.
statements.action_statement: Affects only users of Liquibase Secure 5.0.0, 5.0.1 or 5.0.2 who extract and start the license-tracking application. Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 5.0.3 or later, whose license-tracking application bundles a fixed Tomcat. Until then, start the application with SPRING_SERVLET_MULTIPART_ENABLED=false, or do not run it.

statements.status_notes: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. Tomcat did not validate that the host name provided via the SNI extension was the same as the host name provided in the HTTP host header field. If Tomcat was configured with more than one virtual host and the TLS configuration for one of those hosts did not require client certificate authentication but another one did, it was possible for a client to bypass the client certificate authentication by sending different host names in the SNI extension and the HTTP host header field. The vulnerability only applies if client certificate authentication is only enforced at the Connector. This issue affects Apache Tomcat from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.14, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.49, from 9.0.0-M1 through 9.0.112, and 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.15 or later, 10.1.50 or later or 9.0.113 or later, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Client certificate authentication bypass through mismatched SNI and Host header names, fixed in Tomcat 11.0.15, 10.1.50 and 9.0.113. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2 and 10.1.48 in 5.0.3, both in range; 5.1.0 and later carry 11.0.15 or newer, which include the fix. The bypass needs a TLS connector serving more than one virtual host, with client certificate authentication required on the connector for one host but not another. The application sets no server properties, so its embedded Tomcat runs one default host over plain HTTP with no TLS connector and no client certificate authentication, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer.

Incomplete OCSP verification in Tomcat's FFM/OpenSSL TLS integration. Requires an active TLS listener with client certificate authentication and OCSP validation configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or binds any TLS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; the TLS and OCSP subsystems are never initialized.

HTTP request/response smuggling via invalid chunk extension in Tomcat HTTP/1.1 parser. Requires an active HTTP listener processing inbound requests. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; the HTTP parser is never invoked.

statements.status_notes: Occasional URL redirection to untrusted Site ('Open Redirect') vulnerability in Apache Tomcat via the LoadBalancerDrainingValve. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.18, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.52, from 9.0.0.M23 through 9.0.115, from 8.5.30 through 8.5.100. Other, unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.20, 10.1.53 or 9.0.116, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Occasional open redirect in Tomcat's LoadBalancerDrainingValve, fixed in Tomcat 11.0.20, 10.1.53 and 9.0.116. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 10.1.48 in 5.0.3, 11.0.15 in 5.1.0 and 11.0.18 in 5.1.1, all in range; 5.2.0 and later carry 11.0.22 or newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs LoadBalancerDrainingValve to be explicitly added to the server's pipeline, on a cluster node that a load balancer has put in the draining state. Tomcat never installs the valve by default and Spring Boot never configures it. The application sets no server properties, and none of its classes references a Tomcat valve, the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer.

TLS 1.3 cipher suite preference order not preserved in Tomcat's SSL connector configuration. Requires an active TLS connector performing cipher negotiation. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or binds a TLS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no TLS handshakes occur.

statements.status_notes: Apache Tomcat authentication bypass where OCSP validation soft-fails even when soft-fail is explicitly disabled, allowing revoked client certificates to authenticate.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass due to CLIENT_CERT soft fail misconfiguration in Tomcat's OCSP validation. Requires an active HTTPS connector configured with CLIENT_CERT authentication and an OCSP responder. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No connector, no authenticator, no OCSP — the code is inert.

Information disclosure via padding oracle vulnerability in Tomcat EncryptInterceptor (clustering component). Requires Tomcat clustering with EncryptInterceptor enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; EncryptInterceptor is never instantiated.

statements.status_notes: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat due to an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66614. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.15 through 11.0.19, from 10.1.50 through 10.1.52, from 9.0.113 through 9.0.115. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.20, 10.1.53 or 9.0.116, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66614, fixed in Tomcat 11.0.20, 10.1.53 and 9.0.116: the strict check that the TLS SNI host name matches the HTTP Host header ignored differences in case, so it could be bypassed. It matters only when Tomcat terminates TLS itself with more than one SSLHostConfig, one of which requires client certificate authentication at the Connector while another does not. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. Only 5.1.0 (11.0.15) and 5.1.1 (11.0.18) carry an in-range version. 5.0.0 to 5.0.2 (10.1.34) and 5.0.3 (10.1.48) predate the strict SNI check, which the CVE-2025-66614 fix added in 10.1.50, and 5.2.0 and later carry 11.0.22 or newer, which include the fix. The application listens on a single plain HTTP connector with the Spring Boot defaults: it sets no server properties, ships no keystore, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API, an SSL bundle or a web server factory customizer.

Information disclosure via improper encoding in Tomcat JsonAccessLogValve. Requires an active HTTP connector with JsonAccessLogValve configured and non-default relaxedPathChars/relaxedQueryChars values. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no access log valves are configured or initialized.

Information disclosure via sensitive data in Tomcat log files from the Kubernetes cloud membership provider (clustering). Requires Tomcat clustering with Kubernetes membership enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; Kubernetes cluster membership is never initialized.

statements.status_notes: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117. Older, unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version [FIXED_VERSION], which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Unbounded request body reads in Tomcat WebDAV LOCK and PROPFIND handling affect Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. The license utility pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.21 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26, tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:52) through spring-boot-starter-web (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:60) and starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20), but no WebDAV servlet, WebDAV mapping, or PROPFIND/LOCK handler is configured in tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main or its application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1).

statements.status_notes: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat: HTTP/2 request headers were not validated, which may have triggered unexpected application behavior. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 10.0.0-M1 through 10.0.27. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: HTTP/2 request header validation gap in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires HTTP/2 connections to a running Tomcat server. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not enable HTTP/2 — application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) sets no server.http2.enabled property and declares no HTTP/2 connector, and the codebase contains no HTTP/2-specific Tomcat configuration. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26), so the fixed version is installed regardless.

statements.status_notes: Exposure of HTTP Authentication Header to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.2 through 9.0.117, 8.5.24 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.83 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: Exposure of HTTP authentication headers to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires a WebSocket client following an HTTP redirect during authentication. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not use the Tomcat WebSocket client or server APIs. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no WebSocket endpoint definitions, and the codebase contains no ClientEndpoint/ServerEndpoint annotations or other WebSocket-related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

statements.status_notes: Authentication Bypass Issues vulnerability in digest authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass in Tomcat digest authentication, where any unknown user presenting the password "null" was authenticated. Affects Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires Tomcat to be configured to use DigestAuthenticator. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not configure any Tomcat realm or authenticator. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no realm/authenticator definitions, and the codebase contains no DigestAuthenticator or related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

statements.status_notes: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity in LockOutRealm in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: LockOutRealm treats user names as case-sensitive, reducing its effectiveness against brute-force attacks. Affects Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires Tomcat to be configured to use LockOutRealm. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not configure any Tomcat realm. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no realm definitions, and the codebase contains no LockOutRealm or related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

statements.status_notes: Observable Timing Discrepancy vulnerability when comparing AJP secret in Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Older unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.22, 10.1.55 or 9.0.118 which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Non-constant-time comparison of the AJP connector secret, a timing side channel that lets an attacker on the local network recover the secret; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.22, 10.1.55 and 9.0.118. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 10.1.48 in 5.0.3, 11.0.15 in 5.1.0 and 11.0.18 in 5.1.1, all in range; 5.2.0 and later carry 11.0.22 or newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs an AJP connector configured with a secret. Spring Boot exposes no property that enables AJP and starts only an HTTP connector; an AJP connector must be added in code through a web server factory customizer. The application sets no server properties, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API, a connector or a web server factory customizer. A source review found no AJP connector configuration anywhere in this repository.

Repo-wide searches found no source declaration for org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core; the only Tomcat references in the current tree are prior VEX notes. The active build declares unrelated dependencies such as httpcore5 5.4.3 in pom.xml:121-122 and jackson-core 2.22.1 in pom.xml:57,150-151 and community-extensions/liquibase-mongodb/pom.xml:48,90-92.

statements.status_notes: Always-Incorrect Control Flow Implementation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's rewrite valve meant that if the first condition in an OR chain matched, subsequent non-OR conditions were skipped. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.22, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.55, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.118, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Other versions that have reached end of support may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.23, 10.1.56 or 9.0.119, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: In Tomcat's RewriteValve, if the first condition in an OR chain matched, the non-OR conditions after it were skipped, so a rewrite rule could apply when it should not; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.23, 10.1.56 and 9.0.119. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.1 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.1 and 5.0.2, 10.1.48 in 5.0.3, 11.0.15 in 5.1.0, 11.0.18 in 5.1.1 and 11.0.22 in 5.2.0, all in range; 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 carry 11.0.23 and 11.0.24, which include the fix. The flaw needs a RewriteValve with rewrite rules. Spring Boot exposes no property that enables one; it must be added in code through a web server factory customizer. None of the application's classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer, and the application ships no rewrite configuration.

statements.status_notes: Always-Incorrect Control Flow Implementation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat meant that special roles and empty authorisation constraints were not included when the effective web.xml was logged. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.22, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.55, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.118, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Other versions that have reached end of support may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.23, 10.1.56 or 9.0.119 which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: When Tomcat logs the effective web.xml of a web application, the logged copy left out special roles and empty authorization constraints; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.23, 10.1.56 and 9.0.119. The flaw is in the logging output only, and it shows only when the Context's logEffectiveWebXml option is enabled. That option is off by default. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.1 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.1 and 5.0.2, 10.1.48 in 5.0.3, 11.0.15 in 5.1.0, 11.0.18 in 5.1.1 and 11.0.22 in 5.2.0, all in range; 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 carry 11.0.23 and 11.0.24, which include the fix. The application has no web.xml and never enables logEffectiveWebXml: Spring Boot exposes no property for it, and none of the application's classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer. Its security constraints are therefore never logged, so the incomplete log output cannot occur.

statements.status_notes: Improper Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat leads to security constraints specified for the default servlet ignoring any method or method omission configured as part of the constraint. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.22, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.55, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.118, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other versions that have reached end of support may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.23, 10.1.56 or 9.0.119, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Security constraints that Tomcat applied to the default servlet ignored any HTTP method or method omission configured in the constraint; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.23, 10.1.56 and 9.0.119. Exploitation requires an application that maps Tomcat's default servlet and protects it with method-specific security constraints. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.1 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz); it runs only if a user extracts and starts it. 6.0.0 and 6.0.1 contain no Tomcat. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 (5.0.1, 5.0.2), 10.1.48 (5.0.3), 11.0.15 (5.1.0), 11.0.18 (5.1.1) or 11.0.22 (5.2.0), which are in range; 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 carry 11.0.23 and 11.0.24, which include the fix. The application declares no security constraints at all: it has no web.xml, no servlet security annotations or registrations, no Spring Security library, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API. It sets no server properties, so Spring Boot's default of not registering Tomcat's default servlet applies.

statements.status_notes: Missing Critical Step in Authentication vulnerability in Apache Tomcat when the JNDIRealm was configured to authenticate binds using GSSAPI allowed attackers to authenticate without provided the correct password. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.4, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.36, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.100, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.5, 10.1.37 or 9.0.101, which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Tomcat's JNDIRealm, when configured to authenticate its LDAP binds with GSSAPI, could authenticate a user without the correct password; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.5, 10.1.37 and 9.0.101. Exploitation requires a JNDIRealm configured for GSSAPI binds. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.1 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz); it runs only if a user extracts and starts it. 6.0.0 and 6.0.1 contain no Tomcat. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.1 and 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The application never configures a Tomcat realm of any kind: Spring Boot does not set up a realm for the embedded Tomcat, the application has no server properties, no web.xml and no web server factory customizer, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API. It bundles no LDAP, Kerberos or Spring Security library.

statements.status_notes: Improper Access Control, Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat leads to security constraint bypass if a constraint for a longer path is specified before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58, 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Security constraint bypass when a `<security-constraint>` for a longer path is declared before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path in web.xml. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container evaluating security constraints against deployed web.xml descriptors. Liquibase is a CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No servlet container is started, so no security-constraint evaluation ever occurs.

statements.status_notes: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat due to incomplete fix for CVE-2026-32990. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.20 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.53 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.115 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-32990: an HTTP/2 request without an :authority pseudo-header could bypass Tomcat's strict check that the TLS SNI host name matches the requested host; fixed in 11.0.25, 10.1.59 and 9.0.121. It matters only when Tomcat terminates TLS itself, has HTTP/2 enabled on that connector, and serves more than one SSLHostConfig with differing client certificate requirements. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz), and it runs only if a user extracts and starts it; the image entrypoint runs the Liquibase CLI. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. Only 5.2.0 (11.0.22), 5.2.1 (11.0.23) and 5.2.2 (11.0.24) carry an in-range version; 5.0.0 to 5.0.3 (10.1.34, 10.1.48) and 5.1.0 and 5.1.1 (11.0.15, 11.0.18) are below the affected ranges. The application listens on a single plain HTTP connector on port 8080 with the Spring Boot defaults: its configuration sets no server.ssl or server.http2 properties, so neither TLS nor HTTP/2 is enabled, it ships no keystore, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API, an SSL bundle or a web server factory customizer.

statements.status_notes: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator. If, before windowSize requests have been made, a client makes a DIGEST authenticated request with a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window then that request is replayable once only while the associated nonceCount remains within the replay window. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass by capture-replay in Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator: a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window can be replayed once before it ages out. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with DIGEST authentication configured and processing inbound authenticated requests. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No DIGEST authenticator is ever configured or invoked.

statements.status_notes: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows the bypassing of a security constraint that limits user access to a resource via POST but not GET. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Incorrect Authorization in Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows bypassing a security constraint that limits a user to POST access on a resource (not GET). Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with FORM authentication and a POST-only security constraint configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No FORM authenticator or security constraint is ever configured.
